newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares firm 0.55 pct, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares firm 0.55 pct, off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares lost most of their earlier gains in flat afternoon trade on Thursday due to a persisting lack of fresh liquidity inflow, brokers said.
They said ongoing cash shortage in the money markets continued to squeeze the bourse amid high overnight rates.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 2,016, up 11 points, or 0.55 percent from Wednesday after brushing an early high of 2,047.
Daily volume rose 41.9 percent to 21.81 trillion lira ($133 million), from Tuesday's 15.4 trillion ($94 million).

"There is definitely no cash entry. So, bearish sentiment quickly gripped the market again in the afternoon after a vivid morning. There's no hope for the index to exceed its trading record of 2,070 with the present volume," said Mehmet Aksoy from Gedik Securities.

Turkish central bank continued to fund banks on overnight and tomorrow value ahead of Friday's hefty public sector salary payments. The average overnight money and repo rates ended little changed at 73.79 and 79.79 percent, respectively.

"The index may move up a bit further if fuelled by news from the political front and may pass 2,070, but this would be a fake move with the current turnover. Investors must be careful not to get caught up in such a bullish trap," said Erol Dalak from Ata securities.
